articles.body:
The midfielder had agreed a deal to join the Magpies in the summer before a late bid saw him move to the Midlands instead, and he has impressed since making his debut.

He scored in the Champions League against Fernerbahce in midweek - on his 21st birthday - and continued his hot streak when he nodded home the only goal of the game in the 36th minute.

"I knew this team was very good. I played against them in the Europa League final last season. I knew it was a very good team with a big coach. I knew that it was perfect for me," Manzambi told Sky Sports after the game.

In conceding, Newcastle set a new club record of 16 successive games in all competitions in which they have failed to keep a clean sheet.

It came shortly after a controversial moment when Sven Botman should have been sent off. He was initially shown a yellow card for a reckless challenge on Nicolas Jackson, but VAR reviewed it for serious foul play. However, they decided not to upgrade the booking and Botman remained on the pitch.

"If VAR can't see that's a red, we're in trouble," Sky Sports ' Jamie Redknapp said at half-time. "It is so dangerous. How he's not broken his leg there... I like to see aggression. I want to see 50/50 tackles, but you can't do that anymore."

After the game, Jackson told Sky Sports: "The referee said it was a yellow card but it was so high. Hopefully next time it is a red card. I nearly broke my leg, but it's fine. It's part of football."

However, Newcastle ultimately ended the first half with no shots on target. There were some better openings in the second half for the Magpies - including a wonderful save from Zion Suzuki to deny Botman - but that proved to be their only shot on target in a game where they lacked the final touch.

Newcastle were loudly booed at both half-time and the final whistle as the team's stuttering start under Matthias Jaissle continued.

Aston Villa were also guilty of not finishing their chances but looked far more like the team Unai Emery wants. The three points sends them level on eight points with Newcastle and just a place behind.

9: CHANCE! Jackson is through on goal but his shot goes straight at Lukas Hornicek.

18: YELLOWS! Joelinton and Botman are both booked for hefty challenges, with a VAR review for Botman's foul on Jackson.

20: NO RED! VAR do not see a clear and obvious error and Botman does not receive a red card.

29: CHANCE! Jackson has another chance to score, but his effort comes off Botman's backside.

35: GOAL! Manzambi rises high to nod home Gomes' cross for Villa's opener.

39: OFF THE POST! Emi Buendia almost makes it two for Aston Villa, but hits the post.

49: HUGE SAVE! Botman's thunderous strike is pushed away by Suzuki's fingertips.

73: SAVE! From Hornicek this time as he pushes Ross Barkley's shot away.

Jaissle: 'We were dominating, we just couldn't score'

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle speaking with Sky Sports: "It was a game where we were dominating. Overall I thought I was seeing a team giving a response.

"We had many situations where you saw that we were going to win that game and then we conceded a goal.

"We also need to be honest. We were shaky until half-time but then after that we showed a good response after half time.

"The second 45 minutes were again really aggressive. We won the important duels. Unfortunately we were just not smart enough in our decision making in the final third so that is something we need to improve.

"There were many occasions where we didn't find the right pass. Sometimes not the right timing. These things need to be combined pretty soon to be more efficient."

On Botman challenge: "It was really fast. The decision-making was clear from the referee. They even checked [VAR] the foul from Sven."

Mings: We're slowly grinding towards cohesion

Aston Villa captain Tyrone Mings to Sky Sports: "It was a perfect away Premier League performance. St James' Park is so difficult to come to, but you're see across the board that every game in the league at the moment is so difficult.

"It feels like a big win. I'm super proud of everything we've put into the season so far.

"It feels at times like we've had a lot of changes but the manager is keen to reiterate we have a 'no excuse'. We have enough players here who have experience playing at St James' Park and have experienced the league and we've added some fantastic players. Coming here is always difficult, but I'm super proud to keep a clean sheet.

"It feels like we're slowly grinding towards cohesion, but there's no other way than hard work.

"We've just had quite a long international break where players were away, but some were here and working hard but every day on the training pitch, in meetings, everybody is buying in to what the manager wants, how he wants to play.

"The league is tough, the standard is tough, we're playing in Europe is tough but that's the tough we want. We want to be up there, we want to play European football. This is the challenge we chose and we're super excited for the season."

Emery pleased as Aston Villa improvement continues

Aston Villa head coach Unai Emery to Sky Sports: "Hard, tough match, but the victory is fantastic. How we compete, how we play when we need it defensively, to feel in our structure, everybody, the commitment we needed.

"We were working on it in previous matches, in our analysis of how we needed to play, our game plan. Then we could have possibilities as well to dominate, sometimes with the ball possession.

"Try to impose with our positioning, try to use our skills, our game plan as well in transition sometimes, sometimes through keeping ball possession to stop them as well and to try to dominate.

"We did it in 90 minutes more or less, more in transition, but we defended well. We conceded not so many chances and we had a very good opportunity to score the second goal to finish the game.

"But how we are improving, how we are competing, how we are being aware, the things we need to work, I think is the most important how we did today."

articles.title: Nick Saban and Tim Tebow give their thoughts on expanding the College Football Playoff to 24 teams
articles.summary: Nick Saban says there aren't 24 College Football Playoff teams that can win a title, warning bowl games and the SEC Championship Game face extinction.

There's not 24 teams in the country that deserve to be in the playoffs," he started. "I don't think there's 24 teams in the country that can win the championship." articles.title: Ryan Coleman-Williams Injury Update, Latest on Alabama WR's Return Timeline After Reported Surgery
articles.summary: Alabama could be without Ryan Coleman-Williams for multiple weeks after the star wide receiver underwent arthroscopic knee surgery on a meniscus injury, ESPN's Katie George reported Saturday (h/t ESPN's Alex Scarborough).
articles.body:
Alabama could be without Ryan Coleman-Williams for multiple weeks after the star wide receiver underwent arthroscopic knee surgery on a meniscus injury, ESPN's Katie George reported Saturday (h/t ESPN's Alex Scarborough ).

"While the timeline for his return is unclear, sources told ESPN that Coleman-Williams is considered week-to-week," Scarborough reported.

Coleman-Williams had already been ruled out for Saturday's game against Tennessee with what coach Kalen DeBoer confirmed were knee and head injuries.

"He's been dealing with a meniscus injury the past three weeks, playing through it, but ultimately (doctors) wanted to go in, get it cleaned up, so he had it scoped," George said about Coleman-Williams during ABC's Saturday broadcast of Texas' matchup against Florida (h/t AL.com's Creg Stephenson ).

George added, per Stephenson: "We're told that he's doing well, but we're not likely going to see him for the next couple of weeks."

Coleman-Williams had previously played with a knee brace for two games for what he initially described as "precautionary reasons," per the Associated Press .

The wide receiver was forced to leave last week's matchup against Georgia following a helmet-to-helmet hit in the fourth quarter.

The helmet hit marked the second time Coleman-Williams left the game against the Bulldogs. He briefly exited the game after landing awkwardly after jumping to attempt a catch in the second quarter.

DeBoer told reporters and Monday Coleman-Williams was deadling a "head issue" as well as the lingering knee problem and would likely be considered week-to-week going forward.

Coleman-Williams, who is playing in his third season with the Crimson Tide, had recorded 23 catches for 415 receiving yards with four touchdowns as Alabama's top receiver through his first six games of the season.

Cederian Morgan and Noah Rogers could both get more look from starter Keelon Russell as Alabama looks to give Coleman-Williams enough time to heal both from his knee procedure and his head injury.

articles.title: Aaron McLean's EFL takeaways: West Ham unstoppable, Norwich in trouble
articles.summary: BBC Final Score pundit Aaron McLean looks at the weekend's talking points in the EFL, including West Ham win over in-form Swansea City and Norwich City's woes.
articles.body:
Former Peterborough United and Hull City striker - and Final Score pundit - Aaron McLean gives his five takeaways following Saturday's action in the Championship, League One and League Two.

West Ham look unstoppable after statement win at leaders Swansea

West Ham won their fixture with Swansea City in the Championship, thanks to Divine Mukasa's goal, and have moved to within a point of the Welsh club at the top of the table. They've scored a remarkable 30 goals in their 11 league games.

McLean: "I think it was a huge win for West Ham. Take nothing away from Swansea and I think the start they've had has been incredible, but today was always going to be a real test for them.

"After the demolition of Lincoln in midweek, it was important West Ham backed that up with three points to close the gap to just one point behind Swansea and they did that.

"I think once West Ham go back top of the league, they probably won't come off it again.

"I think the fact that Middlesbrough drew today made it even more of a reason why they needed the three points.

"Jarrod Bowen has got eight goals and keeping him was probably the best thing that could have happened for West Ham.

"There were a lot of questions asked about him and if he had gone to the World Cup, and he was a regular in the England squad, I think maybe it might have been different.

"I think the fact he wasn't selected was a huge reason why he was like, 'No, I'm captain of this football club and and I want to help get them back to the Premier League'."

Norwich don't seem to have 'an ounce of recovery in them'

Portsmouth's Marezi converted a penalty to send Norwich City crashing to a sixth straight loss, leaving them just one point above the relegation zone when their fans had expected them to mount a promotion bid.

McLean: "I've got egg on my face because they were my wild promotion pick so I'm as surprised as anyone that they're doing so badly.

"I thought the job Philippe Clement did when he came in last year was incredible and I really fancied them to kick on this season and not only challenge for the play-offs, but challenge for automatic promotion and be right up there.

"They've just been so disappointing and they look void of any confidence at the moment. I don't know where they go from here.

"With each game they lose, you can see the confidence streaming out of the squad. As soon as they concede a goal, you think 'here we go again'. It's like groundhog day.

"The goalkeeper [Daniel Grimshaw] is under a lot of pressure as well, he's not having the best of seasons. The goals they're conceding, some of those are easily avoidable.

"So, yeah, I think over the next couple of weeks, there are going to be huge questions asked, not only of the goalkeeper, but of Clement.

"It's not so much that they're losing games, I think it's that they're consistently losing. Good teams show they can recover, but at the moment, Norwich don't look like they've got an ounce of recovery in them."

It remains to be seen if Watford have turned a corner

Watford ended a miserable run of four straight losses, which looked like it would cost Alessio Dionisi his job, by winning 2-0 against Charlton and they are now three points above the relegation zone.

McLean : "That was a huge win for Watford against Charlton and they needed that, but I wouldn't say they've turned a corner just yet.

"The timing of the Charlton game was perfect for Watford and it was the right game at the right time.

"Charlton came into that game having not won in seven games. They were understandably low on confidence.

"I think it was just two out-of-form teams up against each other, and fortunately for Watford, they came out on the right side of it.

"That's especially true for the manager, Alessio Dionisi, and he desperately needed that result. I would have feared for him past this weekend if they had lost again, especially given how poorly they played against Cardiff in midweek, when they conceded five.

"I think it is a stepping stone, but I still think that the ownership are going to need a lot of convincing.

"They've shown in the past they're not scared to make changes and Dionisi is going to need a run of results if he's going to remain in his position."

A first league win can be huge for Paul Warne and MK Dons

After drawing six of their opening eight League One games, MK Dons finally beat Luton Town 2-1 to get their first league win under manager Paul Warne.

McLean : "It was a brilliant result first and foremost. You know Luton are a team that are expected to be up there challenging.

"Jack Wilshere will be feeling the pressure that they're expected to be challenging for promotion.

"But I think what MK Dons have got on their side is that Paul Warne is a vastly experienced manager at League One level.

"So he knows how to get results. At the moment they're probably not getting the wins he would like, but I think that will change now.

"He took them up from League Two last season and I think he will get them going again. It will take them a little bit of time to get going and to really gel, but I think they'll be fine.

"I think as the season progresses, they'll get stronger. The team will have a lot more cohesion and I expect them to be comfortable at least in mid-table."

A baptism of fire for Alex Bruce at Rotherham

Alex Bruce is enduring a tough first job in management and his Rotherham United side have slipped into the bottom two in League Two after losing 2-0 at Fleetwood.

McLean: "I think when you look at Rotherham and Crawley, the other team at the bottom of League Two, they've both got managers who are in charge for the first time.

"That lack of experience in these types of moments is showing. That's not to say that given time they won't be able to come through, but the problem they've got is the average lifespan of a manager in the EFL isn't very long, it's about nine months.

"So I do think they'll both be worried and I don't think either team has the strongest of squads.

"I'd say Rotherham out of the two will be the ones who really need to put a run of form together and move up with the players they've got.

"They were in League One last season and they're underachieving.

"In Alex Bruce's defence, he hasn't been given the money to be able to go and improve the squad, so it's very hard.

"He needs to galvanise the squad, and they need to just grind out a few results. They need to try and get themselves above that line. Today was a bad day, but it's nothing a few good results can't change."

Aaron McLean was speaking to BBC Sport England's David Anderson.

articles.title: Julian Sayin Injured, Latest Updates on Ohio State QB's Status After Exit vs. Indiana
articles.summary: Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin will miss multiple weeks after landing on his shoulder following a hit in the fourth quarter of Saturday's 19-15 win over Indiana, head coach Ryan Day revealed after the game.
articles.body:
Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin will miss multiple weeks after landing on his shoulder following a hit in the fourth quarter of Saturday's 19-15 win over Indiana, head coach Ryan Day revealed after the game.

"I don't have a ton of details, but he'll probably be out for several weeks," Day told reporters (h/t Fox's Trey Wallace). "So, we'll have to come up with a plan there."

Sayin left the game before returning to the sideline with no helmet and his right arm in a sling.

Quarterback Luke Fahey came in to replace Sayin with seven and a half minutes left in the game. No. 4 Ohio State held a 19-15 lead over No. 5 Indiana at the time.

Fahey did not complete a pass on two attempts. He also lost two yards on two carries.

Indiana had a shot at extending the team's 22-game winning streak when Josh Hoover attempted a touchdown pass from fourth and four with just over a minute remaining, but wide receiver Nick Marsh was ruled out of bounds on the potential game-winning catch.

Ohio State is scheduled for a Week 8 bye before returning Oct. 31 for a road game against USC.

The Buckeyes could be heading into that matchup with a quarterback depth chart led by Fahey, a true freshman, and Tavien St. Clair, who is in his second season with the program and competed with Fahey for the backup job earlier this season.

Buckeyes wideout Jeremiah Smith said he felt the upcoming bye could help him build chemistry with Fahey by Ohio State's next game.

"Two weeks 'til we play a game, so it's going to take time to build that," Smith told reporters Saturday (h/t Cleveland.com's Stephen Means). "I ain't going to say it's going to take one day. It's not that easy."

Sayin had started all six games of Ohio State's 5-1 start, completing 71.2 percent of his passes with 1,772 passing yards and 17 touchdowns with two picks.

He struggled early in Saturday's matchup against Indiana, going 15-for-29 with 235 yards and throwing multiple interceptions for the second straight game prior to his injury.

Hoover, who also saw mixed results in Saturday's loss, missed one play earlier in the game after landing on his right shoulder in the third quarter. Indiana will hope to get better news about his health before the Hoosiers' matchup at Michigan next weekend.

articles.title: Pellegrini: "Decisiones absolutamente inentendibles e inexplicables"
articles.standfirst: El chileno explota contra el arbitraje de De Burgos Bengoetxea
articles.summary: El chileno explota contra el arbitraje de De Burgos Bengoetxea
articles.body: Manuel Pellegrini hacía una primera valoración de la derrota del Betis frente al Barcelona en La Cartuja en los micrófonos de DAZN. "La sensación es de impotencia, sin lugar a dudas. Perder este partido 2-5 no refleja lo que ocurrió. Hubo una serie de incidencias con decisiones del árbitro absolutamente inentendibles e inexplicables. Y una expulsión que nos dejó en inferioridad en una jugada absurda. La mano es Cucho es fruto del empujón del jugador del Barcelona", afirmaba el técnico verdiblanco. Y continuaba: "Lo empuja y no tiene incidencia en una jugada que está a treinta metros del gol. Y en el tercer gol de ellos, el jugador de ellos pone el pie a la altura de la cabeza y el VAR no lo revisó. Finalmente, la expulsión es una provocación y un empujón de Lamine a la que responde Facundo. Se le llama la atención a los dos y se les enseña amarilla y listo. Hubo incidencias muy importantes y lamentablemente nos vimos perjudicados siempre nosotros". Gol anulado. "Cucho va a parar el balón con el pecho, le empujan y le pega con la mano. A 30 metros del gol, no tiene incidencia ninguna. No es que se haya acomodado la mano el Cucho. Creo que eso limita el espectáculo, 60.000 personas cuando el equipo ha jugado muy bien". Lo Celso y Ceballos. "Son muy importante para nosotros. Teníamos la idea de tener más la pelota con Fornals, Ceballos... Empatamos, tuvimos el 2-1 con esa ocasión de Bellerín y luego vinieron las incidencias, sobre todo la expulsión, y ya se desequilibró el partido". Orgullo. "Si logramos jugar de igual a igual ante el Barcelona cuando éramos once contra once... No es fácil. Era un partido muy equilibrado. Hasta el 3-2 fue todo muy parejo ante un gran equipo, que sin duda es el mejor del torneo".

articles.title: Ohio State vs. Indiana Box Score, Player Stats, Highlights, Big Ten Standings, AP Poll Predictions
articles.summary: The No. 4 Ohio State Buckeyes went on the road and ended the No. 5 Indiana Hoosiers' 22-game winning streak Saturday with a 19-15 victory at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, Indiana.
articles.body:
The No. 4 Ohio State Buckeyes went on the road and ended the No. 5 Indiana Hoosiers' 22-game winning streak Saturday with a 19-15 victory at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, Indiana.

Despite being a one-loss road team against the undefeated, reigning national champions, the Buckeyes entered Saturday's clash as 3.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Much like last season's Big Ten Championship Game, which Indiana won 13-10 over Ohio State, the latest chapter in the budding rivalry was predicated largely on strong defensive play.

Biggest Disappointments of 2026 CFB Season 😞

Even so, here is a look at how the top offensive players on each team fared on Saturday afternoon:

By virtue of their victory, the Buckeyes moved into first place in the Big Ten standings ahead of the late-afternoon slate of games:

18. Michigan State: 0-4 (CONF), 2-5 (OVR)

Although it is possible Ohio State could stay put at No. 4 in the Associated Press Top 25 Poll should No. 1 Georgia, No. 2 Notre Dame and No. 3 Miami all win, look for OSU to move up one spot to No. 3 after the big victory at Indiana.

As for the Hoosiers, the competitive loss doesn't figure to hurt them much more than a one-spot drop to No. 6.

Ohio State jumped out to an early lead Saturday, as the first offensive drive of the game covered 67 yards over seven plays and culminated in a field goal.

Indiana jumped ahead early in the second quarter, though, when running back Turbo Richard scored a rushing touchdown from seven yards out after the Hoosiers picked off Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin:

Indiana had a chance to extend the lead to 10-3, but kicker Nico Radicic clanged a 32-yard field goal attempt off the upright, which opened the door for Ohio State.

After getting stonewalled multiple times inside the 5-yard line, Ohio State finally got into the end zone with seven seconds left in the first half when Sayin threw a two-yard touchdown pass to running back Bo Jackson on fourth-and-goal:

The Buckeyes entered the locker room with a 10-7 advantage, and the lead grew to six early in the second half thanks to a field goal after Indiana wide receiver Davion Chandler lost a fumble on the second offensive play of the third quarter:

The Ohio State defense continued to come up big on the ensuing drive with safety Jaylen McClain sacking Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover and forcing a fumble on a fourth-down play at the OSU 27-yard line:

The Indiana defense answered right back, though, as safety Amare Ferrell intercepted Sayin for the second time of the game on the next drive:

The Hoosiers failed to capitalize on the turnover, as Radicic missed another field goal, this time from 55 yards out.

To make matters even worse, Hoover landed hard on his throwing shoulder during the drive. He returned after missing one play, but he was clearly favoring the injury when throwing the ball.

After getting bottled up by the Indiana defense for the first three quarters to the tune of just three catches for 30 yards, all-world Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith finally put his stamp on the game.

On a fourth-and-1 at the Indiana 38-yard line, Sayin lofted the ball into the end zone, and Smith came up with it despite being in double coverage:

Ohio State missed the two-point conversion attempt, but the Smith touchdown extended the lead to 12 points early in the fourth quarter.

Indiana answered on the next drive, going 75 yards on just seven plays over two minutes and 16 seconds, ending with a 19-yard touchdown pass from Hoover to wide receiver Nick Marsh:

The Hoosiers also converted the two-point conversion, shrinking the deficit to 19-15.

Sayin got injured on a strip sack on Ohio State's next offensive drive, causing him to leave the game and requiring his throwing arm to be put in sling:

Freshman quarterback Luke Fahey replaced him and was unable to get anything going on back-to-back drives.

Indiana's offense got the ball back with 2:54 remaining in the fourth quarter, trailing by four, and the Hoosiers quickly moved the ball down the field thanks to a 25-yard pass from Hoover to wide receiver Charlie Becker and a roughing the passer call against Ohio State:

On a fourth-and-4 with just over a minute left, Hoover had Marsh wide open down the sidelines, but he led him a bit too much, and Marsh's foot came down out of bounds as he made the catch:

With that, Ohio State survived and won the game, becoming the first team to beat Indiana since December 2024.

While the Buckeyes got the win, there will undoubtedly be concern about Sayin and his status moving forward after leaving due to injury.

Luckily for the Buckeyes, they are on the bye next week before returning to face USC on the road on Halloween.

With regard to Curt Cignetti's Hoosiers, they will try to start a new winning streak next Saturday when they face Michigan on the road.

articles.title: Florian Wirtz delivers for Liverpool - but is playmaker Andoni Iraola's great conundrum?
articles.summary: Florian Wirtz is instrumental as Liverpool return to winning ways in the Premier League, but does he remain boss Andoni Iraola's great conundrum?
articles.body:
Florian Wirtz was instrumental as Liverpool returned to winning ways in the Premier League at Brentford on Saturday, but does the German playmaker remain boss Andoni Iraola's greatest conundrum?

Wirtz has come in for criticism amid his struggles to replicate the form which persuaded the Reds to pay Bayer Leverkusen what was a club record £116m in June 2025.

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard even said this week that the 23-year-old could benefit from being taken out of the team altogether, to overcome what the club's former captain perceives as a lack of confidence.

The key dilemma facing Iraola was again evident in west London on Saturday.

Liverpool bounced back from their first league defeat of the season against Manchester City last weekend by scoring twice in the second half against a Brentford side reduced to 10 men before half-time.

The visitors produced plenty of chances, particularly with their man advantage in the second half when they registered 14 of their total 21 attempts.

Wirtz was at the heart of things in the final third.

The Germany international created more chances from open play (nine) than any other player has managed in a Premier League game over the past six seasons.

The last player to create as many chances in a single game in the competition was Sadio Mane, for Liverpool against Burnley, in January 2021 (also nine).

In an away game, he is the first player to reach that tally in more than 15 years, since Samir Nasri registered 10 for Manchester City against Tottenham in August 2011.

Despite answering his critics with those standout statistics, the impact of his playing style on the dynamic of the team continues to come under scrutiny.

BBC Sport pundit and former Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy believes a midfield which features Wirtz as the number 10 remains a problem as it makes Iraola's side too easy to play against.

"They got the job done. First and foremost, that's another win on the road, which is always positive," Murphy said of Liverpool 's performance.

"But I thought they looked too easy to play against. The spaces are too big.

"They're playing with two wingers and Wirtz at 10, so they're relying heavily on the two midfield players to try and cover so much space.

"It was too easy for Brentford to play out and to get in behind. That would be the biggest concern today for me."

Liverpool stage comeback to win at nine-man Brentford

Haaland scores twice as Man City beat Ipswich

Injured Martinez taken to hospital as Chelsea beat Everton

Following his latest performance, no player has created more chances in the Premier League this season. He is level with Brighton 's Pascal Gross on 18.

He played in Munoz to begin Liverpool 's fightback, meaning Wirtz has assisted in back-to-back games for Liverpool across all competitions for the first time - although this was only his second goal involvement in seven league games this term.

He was at the heart of Liverpool 's attack, with a match-leading 12 final-third entries and 37 passes in the final third.

However, only Milos Kerkez (20) lost possession on more occasions than Wirtz (19) among Liverpool players, and he won just one of his nine duels.

"They don't look solid and don't look together in terms of shape," Murphy said.

"Instead of a number 10, where Wirtz is struggling to impact games, put three midfielders in.

"Always, the priority is foundation, defence, stability, being hard to beat. The other stuff can follow from there.

"At the moment, it just looks a little bit open. Against better teams, you're going to get hurt."

Victory took Liverpool up to fifth in the table, with three wins from their first seven league games under Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot in the summer.

The Spaniard oversaw the Reds' first away league win after conceding first since December 2023, ending a run of 19 winless away games when going 1-0 behind.

But, while striker Alexander Isak returned from injury, Iraola was dealt fresh blows as Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong suffered injuries on Saturday.

Iraola told BBC Sport: "When you come here, you see the results of Brentford at home and you have to be ready for this kind of battle.

"We had a lot of chances. Even at the end, we had some counters where we were three against one and need to finish. When we go 2-1, every throw-in and every free-kick can be a problem.

"We are in a delicate situation with some of the players. We were talking about this run of four games in 10 days, it's very, very demanding.

"We have to rest again because we have another big, big game against Villarreal [in the Champions League on Tuesday]."

articles.title: Steve Sarkisian's Texas Contract Buyout, Details Revealed After Upset Loss to Florida
articles.summary: With No. 7 Texas suffering a 27-24 upset loss to Florida on Saturday, Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian's job security will be murky as long as the team continues to struggle.
articles.body:
With No. 7 Texas suffering a 27-24 upset loss to Florida on Saturday, Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian's job security will be murky as long as the team continues to struggle.

Potentially moving on from Sarkisian would be costly, though.

He has a $50.9 million buyout in his contract, via The Two Deep .

Biggest Disappointments of 2026 CFB Season 😞

Sarkisian previously signed an extension with the school that kept him under contract through the 2031 season in Jan. 2025.

The Longhorns entered the 2026 season with high expectations and appeared to be a top threat to capture a national title after they opened the year with a perfect 4-0 record. The strong start included impressive victories over Ohio State and Tennessee.

Texas sat at No. 1 in the Week 4 AP Top 25 poll .

The Longhorns then suffered a surprising 27-24 defeat against Oklahoma in the Red River Rivalry on Oct. 10 before dropping their second consecutive game on Saturday.

Sarkisian's offense struggled against a Florida defense that has allowed 393.0 total yards per game this season, the worst mark in the SEC.

Texas only recorded 272 yards and 13 first downs against the Gators. The Longhorns also converted just two of 10 opportunities on third down.

Texas quarterback Arch Manning finished 14-of-20 for 173 yards and one touchdown while losing a fumble.

Sarkisian wasn't pleased with his team's performance.

"I have to evaluate everything," Sarkisian said after the game, per Shawn McFarland of the Dallas Morning News . "This will be a long night. Everything means everything."

Texas now owns a 4-2 record with a 1-2 mark against the SEC, sitting at No. 11 in the conference standings.

articles.title: Arch Manning's Hot Seat as Texas QB Discussed by Sarkisian, 'Everything's Going to Be Evaluated'
articles.summary: Texas football has now lost two straight games to unranked opponents by 27-24 scores after falling to Florida on Saturday. Florida scored 24 unanswered points to turn a 17-3 deficit into a 27-17 lead and held on from there.
articles.body:
Texas football has now lost two straight games to unranked opponents by 27-24 scores after falling to Florida on Saturday. Florida scored 24 unanswered points to turn a 17-3 deficit into a 27-17 lead and held on from there.

Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning threw for just 173 yards and one touchdown, and Texas' hopes effectively ended after he was sacked by Florida linebacker Myles Graham, leading to a fumble recovered by Gators defensive back Kanye Clark with 1:54 left.

After the game, Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said the following when asked about Manning's performance.

Biggest Disappointments of 2026 CFB Season 😞

Last week, the Longhorns lost to their arch-rival, the Oklahoma Sooners. During that game, Manning threw a pick-six to defensive back Peyton Bowen that helped tie the game at 24, and he lefter threw an interception to defensive back Courtland Guillory with 19 seconds left. Oklahoma kicker Tate Sandell made a game-winning 49-yard field goal with no time left.

Simply put, the Longhorns have been very inconsistent offensively after beating Texas State 59-7 in the season opener. Manning has only thrown seven touchdowns in five weeks while committing five turnovers (four interceptions, one lost fumble).

Manning entered college football as the top-ranked prospect in the class of 2023, per 247Sports . While he has certainly shown flashes of greatness since becoming the full-time starter last season, Manning's inconsistency has hurt Texas, which was the sport's No. 1 ranked team but might have trouble even making the College Football Playoff at this point.

The Longhorns' road isn't getting any easier, with their next four games against ranked opponents in No. 9 Ole Miss, No. 16 Mississippi State, No. 13 Missouri and No. 22 LSU.

Obviously, Manning's status will be one to monitor given Sarkisian's comments. Texas' backup is redshirt freshman K.J. Lacey, a 4-star class of 2025 prospect from Saraland, Alabama.

Kickoff in Austin next Saturday is set for 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Curt Cignetti Reacts to Indiana's Nick Marsh Failing to Get Foot Down for Go-Ahead TD in Loss to OSU
articles.summary: Indiana coach Curt Cignetti says Saturday's 19-15 defeat to Ohio State was a "tough one not to win" after wide receiver Nick Marsh stepped out of bounds on a potential game-winning catch late in the fourth quarter.
articles.body:
Indiana coach Curt Cignetti says Saturday's 19-15 defeat to Ohio State was a "tough one not to win" after wide receiver Nick Marsh stepped out of bounds on a potential game-winning catch late in the fourth quarter.

"You all saw the last play. We're fourth and 4, we're expecting a house blitz," Cignetti told reporters Saturday. "You never really know. You're rolling the dice. That's our blitz check that we ran."

Cignetti concluded, "We had it, we just didn't make it happen. So, it's a hard one to swallow. Learn from it, and move on."

Cignetti said the Hoosiers made the call after the Buckeyes sacked Josh Hoover in the red zone on a similar blitz in the third quarter.

The failed attempt at a touchdown pass led to the Hoosiers conceding their first loss in 23 games.

"We had so many opportunities to get it done, not only at the end of the game but throughout the game," Cignetti said. "Just too many missed opportunities on offense."

Cignetti continued, "Defense just kept us in and we start making a few plays. It's right there for the taking, and we've got to be able to take that one."

Hoover credited Marsh with running a "good route" on the final play when speaking to reporters after the loss.

"Nick ran a good route," Hoover said (h/t IUSTV's Ethan Bonheur). "I didn't really have time to sit there and see where he was going, so I had to try and put it up in the air, put it to the spot.

"Shoot, it's a game of inches, right? I think Nick played awesome today."

Hoover, who missed one play earlier in the third quarter after landing on his right shoulder, finished the game having gone 20-for-40 with 296 yards and a touchdown.

"When you play quarterback, it's all about getting the ball to the open guy on time, accurately, as quickly as possible," Cignetti said. "So, that's the bottom line on a quarterback... we certainly had a couple of misfires, but [Hoover] made some nice plays, too."

Cignetti was seemingly critical of Hoover's performance, however, when mentioning a second-quarter drive that ended in a missed field goal.

"I was really surprised we didn't make that happen at the end of the half... we put our three of our receivers on the left hash, and they got all the coverage over there," Cignetti said. "Something went wrong on it, but both guys are wide open."

Indiana's pass attack wasn't the only concern in the loss, during which the Hoosiers were held below 75 rushing yards for a second straight game.

Cignetti and the Hoosiers will have a week to regroup before returning to action next Saturday for a road game at Michigan.

articles.title: Arch Manning's Tenure as Texas Starter Should Be Nearing an End
articles.summary: Perhaps we expected too much. Scratch that, of course we expected too much.
articles.body:
Perhaps we expected too much. Scratch that, of course we expected too much.

With the last name Manning, how could we not?

What has become increasingly evident week over week, however, is that Arch Manning will never be what so many wanted him to be, what Texas and its loyal fans expected him to be, and what Steve Sarkisian, despite a mountain of evidence that says otherwise, still says he will ultimately become.

Biggest Disappointments of 2026 CFB Season 😞

At least not now and not at Texas. And rather we continue to explore ways to manifest his growth and development—to truly avoid this current reality a while longer—we should accept what we already know.

It's best for all parties if Manning's tenure at Texas comes to an end one way or another.

Sure, the Longhorns still have a season to finish out. We're not yet at Halloween, and there is plenty of meaningful football to be played. For Texas, which started its season with a thrilling come-from-behind win over Ohio State, it now finds itself on a two-game losing streak.

First, it was Oklahoma. The Sooners shocked the Longhorns in Week 6, thanks in part to two Manning interceptions.

This week, it was Florida's turn. Although the Gators have allowed a combined 83 points over their past two games and were playing with their backup quarterback on the road, Texas still couldn't win.

While the Longhorns struggled to mount any offense, Manning still had a final drive to tie the game or even give his team the lead. On the second play of that drive Manning fumbled the ball and the Gators recovered, sealing a 27-24 victory.

For Texas, its playoff future is now very much foggy. And with tough games still on the schedule and a potential third loss looming, it's possible this outcome will be the one that dooms the Longhorn's season.

For Manning, this performance could be even more significant. If he wasn't questioning his future at the program coming in—and how could he not given how turbulent the last few years have been—this could (and should) serve as the breaking point.

In many respects, we've been building toward this. Through six games, Manning has scored only 11 touchdowns and thrown five interceptions. He's eclipsed 300 yards passing once, and it came during Week 1 against overmatched Texas State.

After the loss to Oklahoma, the questions that have blanketed his collegiate tenure grew louder. Despite what our eyes have told us, his head coach didn't waiver publicly.

"I think if you took the name off the back of his jersey and you said, 'Here's Joe Smith playing quarterback at the University of Texas and here's a guy who's beaten four top-10 ranked teams in his last 13 starts,' we'd be praising the guy," Sarkisian said earlier in the week. "But the expectations are high for him, and he understands that."

Sarkisian has done nothing but defend his player, and he deserves credit for doing so. The reality of these comments, however, couldn't be further from reality.

If 'Joe Smith' was the starter at Texas, he would have been benched by now.

It's difficult to pinpoint exactly where to start when it comes to Manning's issues. His accuracy remains problematic, although he never truly looks comfortable playing the position.

He rushes his reads, he leaves the pocket when he doesn't have to, and he rarely looks to be in a rhythm. It would be one thing if he was still getting his feet wet, but that is not the case. Manning has been on campus for four years now, and these issues are still painfully obvious.

For Manning, it's difficult to know where to go from here. After the season, he could go to the NFL. Given what we've seen, he'd likely be nothing more than a project on a quarterback-desperate franchise.

The days of him being a surefire top five pick have quickly faded. And it seems unlikely we'll ever return to that point again.

He could enter the transfer portal at season's end, which at this point feels like the most likely outcome. Perhaps another coach and situation will be able to unlock what Sarkisian hasn't been able to.

At the very least, even with the lackluster results, teams would welcome the opportunity to try. This would be best for Manning; it would also make sense for Texas. This once-promising football marriage has lost its luster. And there's no salvaging it now.

Perhaps the more pressing question is what to do in this moment. Texas plays Ole Miss next Saturday, and the road won't get any easier. It's fair to wonder if Manning will start that game given the sudden desperation this program finds itself in.

It's even fairer to wonder if he should.

Only days after he feverishly defended his QB, Sarkisian's tune drastically changed in the afterglow of the latest loss.

"We're not playing good offensive football right now," he said . So everything is going to be evaluated."

This feels like a moment. Something has to give, and it sounds like it might. Saturday was simply the tipping point.

What can't happen is more of the same, not after what we just witnessed and all we've seen over the past few years.

Not for Texas and certainly not for Manning.

articles.title: El Athletic vuelve a la Liga igual que la dejó, empatando otra vez sin goles
articles.standfirst: El equipo dejó pasar la oportunidad que le ofreció una primera mitad mejor que el Valencia
articles.summary: El equipo dejó pasar la oportunidad que le ofreció una primera mitad mejor que el Valencia
articles.body: El Athletic regresó a un partido de verdad 28 días después de haber empatado sin goles en San Mamés ante el Alavés. En ese intervalo de tiempo Terzic se ha dedicado a entrenar, jugar frente a la Real en la final de la Euskal Herria Txapela (0-1, Maroan) y tener una vuelta interrumpida una semana atrás en Vallecas, cuando el encuentro se suspendió con sólo 13 minutos de juego. El viaje a Valencia cambió con respecto al de Vallecas porque los leones tuvieron más balón que en el rato que estuvieron en el campo frente al Rayo. Pero también por la composición elegida por Terzic para el once titular: Paredes fue el único de los defensas que repitió. Rincón entró por Areso, Laporte ocupó el lugar de Yeray y Johaneko arrancó como lateral izquierdo en vez de Yuri. El vascofrancés es un tipo agradecido con lo que le dan y su manera de jugar le convierte en un futbolista fácil de destacar. Fue de los mejores en un primer tiempo en el que el Athletic mandó sobre el Valencia. La segunda parte fue más equilibrada porque la propuesta del Valencia fue más intensa que en el tramo inaugural. También porque las pilas de los leones fueron mermando. El Athletic sufrió en lo emocional tras la lesión de Guruzeta, pero también acusó desgaste. Robert Navarro terminó tieso y Berenguer acusó también problemas musculares. El partido permitió el estreno en esta Liga de Rego, que fue uno de los futbolistas empleados por Terzic entrando desde el banquillo. El centrocampista entró al partido en el minuto 63 en el lugar de Galarreta. En el descanso Terzic también decidió otro relevo en el centro del campo y sacó a Jauregizar por Gerenabarrena.

articles.title: La Roma mantiene el pulso con una joya de Castro... en el debut del hijo de Robinho
articles.standfirst: Daniel de Rossi hizo debutar con el Genoa al hijo del exmadridista
articles.summary: Daniel de Rossi hizo debutar con el Genoa al hijo del exmadridista
articles.body: Santiago Castro encontró un gol donde apenas cabía el balón y, rodeado de cuatro defensas, se inventó una vaselina deliciosa que abrió el camino de la victoria de la Roma frente al Genoa (2-0), mantuvo al equipo de Gian Piero Gasperini a dos puntos del Inter y permitió al delantero argentino celebrar su estreno goleador con la camiseta del conjunto romano. Castro, titular por la sanción de Donyell Malen, celebró su primer gol con la camiseta de la Roma con una acción de enorme calidad. Paró el tiempo en el minuto 58, con 0-0 en el marcador y tras un saque de esquina que acabó con el balón en sus botas cuando estaba en el vértice derecho del área pequeña. Encerrado por cuatro adversarios y prácticamente sin espacio para maniobrar, levantó delicadamente la pelota con la derecha para superar al guardameta. Una pequeña obra de arte ejecutada en una baldosa. Santiago Castro encontró el premio a la confianza de Gasperini en una segunda mitad en la que la Roma terminó por imponer su superioridad. En el minuto 68, el canterano Lulli también se estrenó como goleador del primer equipo después de una magnífica acción individual de Matías Soulé, que desbordó a tres rivales por la derecha y remató a portería. El rechace cayó a los pies de Lulli, que marcó con la izquierda desde el interior del área pequeña. Hasta entonces, el Genoa de Daniele De Rossi, que regresó al Olímpico como entrenador rival, resistió las acometidas de un equipo que dispuso de varias oportunidades durante el primer tiempo. Soulé puso a prueba a Bijlow, Koulierakis cabeceó por encima del larguero y Balerdi estrelló un remate contra el travesaño tras un saque de esquina de Pisilli. Poco después, Rodrigo Mora también obligó a intervenir al portero neerlandés. El Genova tampoco renunció al ataque. El Shaarawy, otro ex del Roma, estuvo cerca de aprovechar un error defensivo de Balerdi y, en el minuto 32, conectó un potente disparo desde fuera del área que se estrelló contra el larguero. Los dos equipos alcanzaron el descanso sin goles después de encontrarse con la madera. Después apareció Santiago Castro, se inventó una maravilla ante Osmanjic, Frendrup, Wiafe y Ostigard. Los cuatro jugadores del Genoa fueron testigos de la obra de arte del argentino, que abrió el camino de una victoria con la que su equipo se recuperó de la derrota ante el Real Madrid (3-4) en la Liga de Campeones y de dos empates consecutivos en la Serie A. Llenó de arte los tres puntos con los que el conjunto de Gasperini se mantiene en la pelea por el liderato. Robinho Júnior, hijo del exfutbolista brasileño del Real Madrid y del Milan Robinho, ha debutado en la Serie A con 18 años después de entrar en el minuto 83 del encuentro que enfrentó al Genoa con la Roma en el estadio Olímpico, donde comenzó su aventura en la máxima categoría del fútbol italiano. El joven atacante brasileño, cuyo nombre completo es Robson de Souza Júnior, sustituyó a Junior Messias y disfrutó de sus primeros minutos con el equipo de Daniele de Rossi, que decidió darle una oportunidad después de sus destacadas actuaciones con el conjunto Primavera del club genovés. Robinho Júnior llegó al Génova el pasado verano procedente del Santos, el mismo club en el que comenzó su carrera su padre, mediante una cesión con opción de compra fijada en ocho millones de euros. Inicialmente destinado al equipo juvenil, su rendimiento aceleró su incorporación a los entrenamientos de la primera plantilla. En el Primavera, dirigido por Domenico Criscito, el brasileño marcó dos goles frente a la Atalanta el pasado septiembre y otro contra la Juventus el 11 de octubre, además de participar decisivamente en la victoria por 1-3 frente al conjunto turinés. Su velocidad, su capacidad para el regate y su habilidad con la pierna izquierda despertaron expectativas sobre su futuro. Con el número 21 en la espalda, durante los algo más de diez minutos que disfrutó sobre el césped del Olímpico de Roma Robinho Júnior no pudo influir en el juego de su equipo, derrotado 2-0 por el Roma con los tantos del argentino Santiago Castro y Emanuele Lulli. Nacido el 17 de diciembre de 2007 en Santos, Robinho Júnior también dio sus primeros pasos profesionales en el equipo brasileño, con el que debutó en julio de 2025 frente al Flamengo. Su llegada al fútbol italiano supone una nueva etapa en una trayectoria inevitablemente marcada por las comparaciones con su padre, que jugó en el Real Madrid, el Manchester City y el Milan. Su padre, que conquistó dos Ligas españolas con el Real Madrid y una italiana con el Milan, cumple actualmente en Brasil una condena de nueve años de prisión por una violación cometida en Italia. Su hijo, mientras tanto, inició este sábado su propio recorrido en la Serie A, con el objetivo de construir una carrera al margen de la notoriedad de su apellido.

articles.title: Facundo Bernal pide disculpas por su expulsión: "Debí controlarme"
articles.standfirst: El jugador del Betis vio la roja en la segunda parte por un cabezazo a Lamine
articles.summary: El jugador del Betis vio la roja en la segunda parte por un cabezazo a Lamine
articles.body: Facundo Bernal fue expulsado en el minuto 54 del partido que el Betis y el Barcelona disputaron en La Cartuja y que finalizó con victoria del líder. Según el acta de De Burgos Bengoetxea, "en el transcurso de una confrontación, este jugador sujetó a un adversario (Lamine Yamal) por el cuello y le propinó dos cabezazos en el rostro de forma consecutiva, no estando el balón en juego. El jugador rival no precisó de asistencia médica y pudo continuar el encuentro". En la acción a la que hace referencia, Fermín estaba tendido en el suelo justo en el instante previo al gol de Abde. Los jugadores del Betis, con el meta Álvaro Valles, corrieron a levantar al futbolista del Barcelona del suelo y Lamine Yamal, que estaba cerca de la jugada, acudió a defender a su compañero. Facundo Bernal sujetó por el cuello a Lamine y le soltó un cabezazo que dejó tendido en el césped al azulgrana. Roja a uno y amarilla al otro. El jugador del Betis ha pedido perdón en sus redes sociales. "Quiero pedir disculpas a mis compañeros y a la afición del Real Betis por haber dejado hoy al equipo con un jugador menos. No suelo reaccionar así y debí controlarme en esa jugada. Asumo la responsabilidad y no volverá a ocurrir", ha escrito el uruguayo. Héctor Bellerín ya comentó tras el partido que Facundo Bernal se había disculpado con sus compañeros. "En el vestuario hay plena confianza para decirnos las cosas buenas y malas. Todos cometemos errores. Hay que salir a arreglarlo en el próximo partido, con cabeza fría y demostrando la ambición, la energía y las ganas que tiene este equipo para que todo esto que hemos hecho hasta ahora no se quede reflejado en esa acción. Hay que seguir todos juntos. Estamos haciendo una campaña muy grande y tenemos que seguir ahí arriba", dijo.

articles.standfirst: Arrasate vuelve con un objetivo, ganar y cortar la mala racha rojilla
articles.summary: Arrasate vuelve con un objetivo, ganar y cortar la mala racha rojilla
articles.body: El Osasuna se mide al Racing de Santander (14:00 horas) con el regreso de Jagoba Arrasate al banquillo navarro como principal novedad y el objetivo de poner fin a la mala racha ante unos cántabros que no jugaban en Pamplona desde el año 2014 y que acumulan una mala racha a domicilio Jagoba Arrasate afronta su primer encuentro al frente de Osasuna tras hacerse oficial su regreso el pasado lunes, en sustitución de un Luis Miguel Ramis que no logró dar con la tecla y terminó siendo cesado. La vuelta del técnico vasco, acompañado de los buenos recuerdos de su anterior etapa, ha devuelto la ilusión a la afición rojilla. Arrasate regresa a El Sadar 876 días después de su último partido como local en el estadio navarro, ahora con el reto de cambiar la dinámica del equipo. Jagoba Arrasate será el protagonista del partido, pero Osasuna deberá centrarse en mejorar su juego en un partido trascendental. El técnico de Berriatua redebuta en El Sadar y lo hará recuperando efectivos para la causa como Kike Barja o Raúl Moro. En definitiva, el templo rojillo será una caldera por dos motivos: el recibimiento a una leyenda del club y la obligación de animar a los suyos para salir de la mala racha que atraviesa El Racing busca ante Osasuna sus primeros puntos a domicilio en esta temporada. El conjunto cántabro es fiable como local, pero todavía no ha sumado como visitante. Como en la semana pasada, el Racing se enfrenta a un equipo que estrena entrenador, en este caso Jagoba Arrasate como nuevo técnico de Osasuna, la anterior jornada fue frente al Valencia de Javier Aguirre. Por este motivo la preparación de partido de José Alberto ha sido más complicada. Para este choque el técnico asturiano no podrá contar con Eriksson por lesión y se ha quedado en Santander por decisión técnica Manu Hernando. En el posible once las principales dudas se centran en la línea de tres por detrás del delantero. En principio Íñigo Vicente es fijo y entre Andrés, Pablo y Canales se juegan dos puestos. A Pamplona viajarán 1000 racinguistas en un deslazamiento cómodo para la afición cántabra. Budimir Vs Zabiri. Dos de los bichos de LaLiga, seis goles contra siete, algo más preciso el segundo, en menos tiempo; un clásico el primero con casi todos los goles de su equipo en su haber: poco más hay que decir.

articles.title: Bryce Underwood Benched by Michigan, Replaced by Lloyd Carr's Grandson Tommy vs. Penn State
articles.summary: Michigan benched quarterback Bryce Underwood at halftime of the Wolverines' home game against Penn State on Saturday afternoon.
articles.body:
Michigan benched quarterback Bryce Underwood at halftime of the Wolverines' home game against Penn State on Saturday afternoon.

Underwood completed 5-of-11 passes for 43 yards and two interceptions against 3-3 Penn State, which lost three games (all Big Ten battles) entering Saturday.

PSU held a 3-0 lead at the break after Michigan's five drives ended in three punts and two picks for 80 total yards.

Head coach Kyle Whittingham made clear to CBS Sports' Jenny Dell at halftime that Michigan needed to get going offensively.

Ultimately, Michigan decided to roll with backup quarterback Tommy Carr, the grandson of former Wolverines head coach Lloyd Carr.

Carr, a true freshman from Saline, Michigan, is a 4-star prospect .

Underwood, the No. 1 overall prospect in the class of 2025, has been Michigan's starter for two seasons. Last season, he completed 60.3 percent of his passes for 2,428 yards (7.2 yards per attempt), 11 touchdowns and nine interceptions. He also rushed for 392 yards and six touchdowns for the 9-4 Wolverines, who ultimately finished No. 69 in scoring out of 136 Division I-FBS teams.

This year's offense has regressed. Entering Saturday, the Wolverines were 102nd out of 138 Division I-FBS teams in points per game (23.0). Underwood completed 59.3 percent of his passes for 881 yards (7.8 YPA), five touchdowns and four picks while adding 212 rushing yards and two scores.

Michigan failed to score 20 or more points in four of its five games, with the lone exception being a 52-17 win over UTEP.

Ultimately, Whittingham, in his first season as Michigan's head coach after leading Utah's program for two decades, decided his team needed a change.

Michigan scored two third-quarter touchdowns largely off the strength of its running attack. Bryson Kuzdzal scored a 43-yard TD, and Jordan Marshall added a one-yard score. On the second drive, Carr hit tight end Hogan Hansen for a 22-yard pass and later added a 22-yard run that got called just short of the goal line.

articles.standfirst: El técnico del Valencia destaca la mejoría del equipo tras el 0-0 ante el Athletic, defiende el trabajo de Hugo Duro y pide paciencia con los jóvenes de la cantera
articles.summary: El técnico del Valencia destaca la mejoría del equipo tras el 0-0 ante el Athletic, defiende el trabajo de Hugo Duro y pide paciencia con los jóvenes de la cantera.
articles.body: Javier Aguirre se mostró satisfecho con la imagen ofrecida por el Valencia pese al empate sin goles frente al Athletic en Mestalla. El entrenador blanquinegro restó importancia a la falta de acierto ofensivo después de las ocasiones generadas y aseguró que su principal inquietud pasa por lograr un mayor equilibrio colectivo durante los partidos. Además, respaldó a Hugo Duro tras los pitos recibidos en las últimas jornadas, defendió su decisión de no recurrir a Aimar Blázquez y reclamó paciencia en la gestión de los jóvenes canteranos, aunque elogió especialmente la progresión y el potencial de David Otorbi. ¿Cómo valora la falta de gol? ¿Por qué Aimar Blázquez no tuvo minutos, teniendo en cuenta que Hugo Duro estaba en el banquillo y no había otro delantero puro? "Falta de gol, falta de gol. Tiramos 16 veces, cuatro a portería, y creo que Unai hizo un buen trabajo. Llegamos más que en Santander, fíjate lo que te digo. Yo lo comentaba en la previa: práctica, práctica, práctica. Los delanteros tienen que meter goles, goles. Hacemos muchos trabajos de finalización y la verdad es que lo han hecho bastante bien. Hoy no quiso entrar y el rival también defiende bien. Entre el portero y nuestros fallos, nos faltó gol, pero no estoy preocupado por eso. Me preocupa más defender bien en bloque medio, porque ahí nos quitaron la pelota tanto el Santander como el Atlético. Ojalá encontremos equilibrio durante los 90 minutos y seamos capaces de meter algún gol. Veníamos de tres derrotas seguidas en casa y, por lo menos, hoy sacamos un empate con buen sabor, sobre todo por las últimas sensaciones. Es con lo que me quedo". ¿Le preocupa que al equipo le cueste sacar el balón y termine rifándolo en largo? "No, es así el fútbol. Hay que buscar soluciones y entrenarlo. Los rivales te neutralizan y todos te aprietan arriba. No es fácil. El balón dividido muchas veces no es un 50-50. Hay que hacer movimientos, poner un ancla que pueda prolongar o jugar de cara. Eso se entrena. Es verdad que dimos algún pelotazo sin ton ni son, producto de la buena presión de ellos. Llevamos diez o doce días juntos y el equipo está creyendo, está entendiendo mejor. Mis tres premisas son correr mucho, jugar bien y ganar. La primera la cumplimos, la segunda la cumplimos a ratos y la tercera no pudo ser. Pero creo que estamos en el camino". ¿Cómo está de ánimo tras otro empate y cómo ha visto a los jugadores? "Estoy muy animado. Soy optimista por naturaleza y tengo mucha fe. Además, estoy contento porque la enfermería está casi vacía y ya tengo el plantel casi completo. Veo a los jugadores con rabia porque han sentido que podían ganar los dos partidos. Eso me gusta, porque no hay que conformarse con un buen partido o un empate en casa: hay que pensar en ganar y ganar. Creo que los dos resultados son justos. A ver si la tercera es la vencida." ¿Por qué acabó el equipo sin un delantero de referencia? ¿Habría cambiado algo con Sadiq disponible? "Pensé que no me iban a preguntar eso. Me lo preguntaron en los seis equipos en los que he estado en esta misma situación. Los jóvenes te ayudan, evidentemente, pero esperas también a los jugadores con experiencia y con goles. Mi obligación es tener a todos vivos y alerta, y claro que los chavales cuentan. Ahí está Otorbi dando el máximo, y también cuentan Córdoba, Aimar y Mayol. Son procesos. Cuando el equipo está bien, es más fácil que los jóvenes aparezcan. Cuando está mal, no puedes cargarles toda la responsabilidad. Yo entiendo la pregunta, pero son decisiones de entrenador". ¿Cómo ve a David Otorbi? ¿Cree que está preparado para dar el salto? "Otorbi tiene unas condiciones físicas evidentes: velocidad, capacidad para atacar el espacio y mucho desparpajo pese a ser tan joven. Le cuesta el trabajo táctico y hay que enseñarle a tener esa pausa en la línea de fondo para centrar mejor y elegir entre buscar al portero o el segundo palo. Es un chico distinto, eso es innegable. Es canterano, humilde y está muy atento a los consejos de sus compañeros y del míster. Creo que va a dar muchísimas alegrías a esta afición y a este club". Hugo Duro se marchó entre pitos de Mestalla tras fallar una ocasión clara la semana pasada. ¿Cómo está y ha hablado con él? "No he considerado necesario hablar con él. Tenemos un seguimiento diario en el que valoramos cómo están los jugadores y, cuando veo alguna señal de alerta, voy a preguntarles qué les pasa. Hugo es maduro, tiene experiencia y es el típico delantero de área que juega de espaldas y ayuda al equipo. Tuvo ese cabezazo y trabajó bien, aunque no lo coronó con gol. La afición es soberana. Si considera que ha hecho un mal trabajo y lo despide con pitos o aplausos, ahí no entro. Para mí, Hugo hizo un buen trabajo; simplemente le faltó el gol".

articles.title: Dundee 2-2 Rangers: Callum Jones scores second-half equaliser as Rangers miss chance to replace Celtic at top of Scottish Premiership
articles.summary: Report as Rangers draw 2-2 at Dundee; home side went ahead through Bradley Fink, but Badredine Bouanani hits back for Rangers before half-time; Nico Raskin scores brilliant goal from distance to put Rangers ahead but Callum Jones equalises to earn Dundee a point
articles.body:
Dundee opened the scoring when Rangers failed to deal with a routine long ball, with Bradley Fink capitalising to round the goalkeeper and slide home.

The lead did not last long, though, as Badredine Bouanani cut inside and curled in a stunning equaliser to open his account for Rangers.

Nico Raskin scored the goal of the game when his shot from outside the area went in off the underside of the crossbar.

But Jones then caught Dan Neil dwelling on the ball and nicked it off the Rangers captain to slot home the Dundee equaliser.

Rangers remain second and move one point behind Celtic, who host Hearts live on Sky Sports on Sunday from 2.30pm.

McInnes: We shouldn't need three goals to win

"I thought Dundee's press was good, as expected, and we wanted to try and draw the centre-backs out at times and try and hit spaces and feed our wide players and try and get 1v1.

"We shouldn't need to come away from home and need to score three goals to win a game.

"Two goals should have been enough tonight. We had a few chances when it went to two each.

"Dundee are a good team, but I think we gifted an opportunity there not to take all three points.

"We're disappointed not to come away with three points."

Pressley: We showed grit and determination

"I thought we were outstanding in the first half, really aggressive, controlled a lot of the game.

"We were really strong on second balls, had one or two moments where we should have capitalised and restricted Rangers to very little.

"We obviously expected a reaction from Rangers and they gave that reaction. They put us under a lot of pressure in the second half.

"The game was getting away from us but we never gave up, we kept going and going and (Callum) Jones got his reward for a really strong performance today."

"Dundee are a good team. They're not there [in the table] by fluke or luck.

"They've got a style of play, Steven Pressley has got a group of players willing to run themselves into the ground for him and that's hard to get.

"They put in a shift and even when they're asked to dig in and suffer like they did for the first 20/25 minutes of that second half.

"They then got a second wind and came back at Rangers and asked questions of them.

"A draw was a fair result. It took wonder strikes to get Rangers two goals.

"There was a lack of creativity at the top end of the pitch and it's something they're going to have to improve."
